title: Real-time burst mitigator and adaptive kernel reroute
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sudden microbursts of short-lived requests (e.g., interactive chat pings, agent heartbeats) create transient congestion in the continuous batching pipeline. That leads to kernel contention on GPUs, poor batch packing for long sequences, and p99+ tail latency spikes during prefill->decode transitions.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, low-latency burst mitigation layer that sits in the admission path and: (1) detects microburst patterns, (2) applies adaptive short-window admission smoothing and batch shaping, and (3) signals the kernel scheduler to reroute to lower-contention kernels (or degrade to a faster, lower-memory attention path) for a short duration. The fix should reduce tail latency spikes without materially harming median latency or throughput for steady-state workload.

Scope: Admission control logic, batch shaper heuristics, a kernel-reroute signaling API, and a prototype rollout behind a feature flag. This ticket focuses on the runtime-side changes and integration tests; client API surface remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency during synthetic 10x microburst test reduced by >= 35% compared to baseline
end-to-end median latency change within ±5% under steady-state traffic
no user-visible errors introduced during kernel reroute (graceful fallback verified)
feature gated with runtime flag and rollout knob in console
automated performance regression tests added to CI
design_notes:
Detect microbursts using a short exponential moving average (EMA) over per-GPU queue depth and request inter-arrival times (50ms and 500ms windows). Admission controller applies a thin probabilistic deferral for requests that would otherwise force small, inefficient batches (targeting token manufacturers < 16). Batch shaper will reserve a small fraction of each batch capacity (e.g., 8%) as 'elastic slots' to absorb stragglers without creating new kernel launches.

Kernel reroute: introduce an internal ControlPlaneSignal 'kernel_reroute_hint' attached to the admission token that carries a lightweight enum {NORMAL, LOW_LATENCY_FAST_ATTENTION, LOW_MEMORY_COMPACT_ATTENTION}. Scheduler consults hint with a short TTL (200ms) and temporarily prefers kernels with lower peak memory or lower launch overhead. Use existing kernel-profile metadata to map hint to concrete kernels.

Backpressure policy: ensure that when the admission controller defers, latency SLOs for prioritised traffic (e.g., P0 routes) are respected by allowing priority bypass. Maintain tenant isolation via current tenanted admission fairness mechanisms.

Security: no customer data leaves runtime; control signal is internal and ephemeral.
implementation_plan: 1) Add microburst detector module (EMA windows + threshold tuning) and unit tests
2) Implement probabilistic short-defer admission path and integrate with existing admission interfaces
3) Add elastic-slot reservation to batch shaper and update batch packing algorithm to prefer filling from reserved slots first
4) Implement kernel_reroute_hint in admission token and wire through scheduler decision path
5) Hook feature flag and console controls (initially internal-only)
6) Bench microburst synthetic harness, iterate thresholds, add CI perf tests
7) Submit implementation PR + design doc link, request eng review
test_plan: Unit tests for microburst detector thresholds and EMA calculations
Integration tests for admission path ensuring requests are deferred/allowed correctly under simulated traffic
Synthetic performance tests: 10s microburst at 10x baseline rps with mixed short/long sequences to measure p50/p95/p99
Chaos test: force kernel reroute signal path and verify graceful fallback when kernel selection fails
Canary tests on dedicated pool with production-like load and telemetry collection for 48h
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime feature flag. Start with canary on 5% of dedicated pool traffic for non-critical routes for 24h. If stable, increase to 25% and run A/B test comparing p99 tail latency and token cost. Roll out to all dedicated nodes for selected regions with a kill-switch in console. Gradually enable for hosted API after 2 weeks and quantitative success signals (p99 improvement, no error regressions).
metrics: p50, p95, p99 end-to-end latency (prefill + decode)
risks: Incorrect thresholding could add latency for steady-state short requests (regress median)
Kernel reroute could pick suboptimal kernels increasing token cost or memory pressure
Interaction with tenant fairness could starve low-priority workloads if not tuned
Feature flag complexity: partial rollout could produce hard-to-debug telemetry mix
